bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (no UI), springboard/sdk/src/document.rs (panel pattern), springboard/src/shell/wifi_page.rs:56 (certificate notice text only), docs/privd-protocol.md (privileged-action password gate, OS layer)
summary: Apple's framework is a set of certificate, identity, keychain and authorization panels and views. BifrOSt has none of these panels or views. The keychain store exists as an SDK API for generic passwords only, and the privileged-action password gate lives in the OS daemon layer with no app-facing lock view.

features.feature: Authorization lock view and plug-in views
features.bifrost: docs/privd-protocol.md (password gate with wrong_password and locked_out errors)
features.note: The privileged-action password check exists in the privd daemon. No app-facing lock icon, authorization dialog or plug-in view exists in the SDK or the shell.
No panel that lists certificates. The document panels in springboard/sdk/src/document.rs show the pattern to reuse.

Wave 3 (w3-security-interface, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No trust settings UI and no certificate chain handling in the SDK or shell.

Wave 3 (theme-10, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The Wi-Fi notice is a fixed string, not a certificate view. Nothing displays certificate contents or details.

features.feature: Choose identity panel and table cell
features.note: No identity picker. The keychain API does not store identities, keys or certificates.

Wave 3 (w3-security-interface, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The SDK stores generic passwords for each app. No panel lets the user create a keychain. docs/bifrost-ui.md (Keychain section, around line 422) lists the gaps.

Wave 3 (w3-security-interface, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No UI for keychain settings. Items are available whenever the shell runs and have no access control.

features.apple: SecurityInterface Constants (Plug-in View Keys, SFDisplayViewException), SecurityInterface Enumerations
features.note: These serve Apple's authorization plug-in model and the authorization view. BifrOSt has no plug-in model of that kind.

gaps: No certificate panel, certificate view or certificate trust editor. The shell has no certificate display or trust UI.
No choose-identity panel. Keychain items cannot hold identities, keys or certificates.
No keychain save or settings panel. The keychain SDK has no UI and no user-facing keychain settings.
No authorization lock view for apps. Apps cannot show a padlock or request an admin password through an SDK control; the privd password gate is not exposed to apps.
Apple's documentation notes the SFAuthorization classes now live in Security Foundation. This matrix does not cover them here.
